# SynBio Wizard

SynBio Wizard: A guided, multi-step pipeline for synthetic biology projects, taking users from goal definition to pathway design and chassis selection.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Five-product goal keyword catalog/pathway/chassis ranking, no arbitrary intent compiler.

text: It automates technical decision-making, providing feasibility assessments and assembly recommendations.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Fixed chassis scores/feasibility Gaussian proxy and part-count assembly suggestion.

text: This wizard ensures that genetic designs are built on solid foundations and are ready for standardized laboratory execution and synthesis.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Architecture-only output not ready for lab execution/synthesis validity.

text: SynBio Wizard: A self-evolving, full-stack biological intelligence system that transforms synthetic biology into a programmable, simulation-driven, and continuously learning engineering discipline.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: No self-evolving biological learning engine.

text: Rather than operating as a linear design pipeline, it functions as a constraint-aware biological compiler that decomposes high-level user intent into multi-dimensional optimization problems across genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic layers.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Catalog product matching and separate analytic utilities, not cross-omic intent optimization compiler.

text: Given a natural language objective, the system constructs a design manifold constrained by codon adaptation index (CAI), GC content windows, ribosome binding site (RBS) strength (ΔG folding), promoter kinetics, transcription factor binding affinities, and host-specific metabolic burden.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Codon diversity/GC CAI proxy, dinucleotide RBS energy and Hill promoter/burden, no joint design manifold.

text: It integrates thermodynamic models (e.g., nearest-neighbor RNA folding), enzyme kinetics (Michaelis–Menten, kcat/Km optimization), and flux balance analysis (FBA) to generate pathway architectures that are not only theoretically valid but metabolically feasible under chassis-specific constraints such as ATP cost, redox balance, and precursor availability.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Michaelis-Menten/serial LP and proxy RNA energy, not nearest-neighbor folding or chassis-specific stoichiometric network.

text: At its core, the platform operates as a “biology-as-code” engine, compiling user-defined goals into executable genetic constructs.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Gene/module name dictionaries, no executable genetic constructs.

text: It programmatically generates gene circuits using logic-gate abstractions (AND/OR/NOT via repressors and activators), designs plasmid architectures with modular assembly standards (Golden Gate, Gibson), and simulates transcriptional–translational coupling using stochastic and deterministic models (e.g., Gillespie simulations for noise, ODE-based systems for steady-state dynamics).
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Boolean circuits/architecture plus actual standalone SSA/ODE, no plasmid nucleotide/assembly-compatible sequence.

text: CRISPR modules are integrated at the design layer, enabling automated guide RNA selection using sliding-window + PAM (NGG/NAG) scanning, GC optimization (40–60%), and off-target prediction via mismatch tolerance scoring and seed-region specificity.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Forward-only NGG/NAG enumeration/GC/seed diversity, no genome background off-target mismatch scan in wizard.

text: Variant effect prediction pipelines (VEP-like) annotate mutations with predicted deleteriousness (SIFT, PolyPhen proxies), while structural modules leverage predicted protein conformations to assess folding stability (ΔΔG) and active-site perturbations.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Partial codon table SIFT/PolyPhen proxy and scalar ddG, no predicted conformations/actual active-site structures.

text: The system extends beyond static design by embedding multi-scale simulation pipelines that propagate perturbations from DNA edits to phenotypic outcomes.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Single-codon mutation-to-ddG/flux/phenotype algebra, not coupled multi-scale biological pipeline.

text: A single nucleotide change is mapped to amino acid substitution, structural perturbation (e.g., disruption of hydrogen bonding networks or metal ion coordination), pathway flux redistribution (via constraint-based modeling such as COBRA/FBA), and ultimately cellular phenotypes such as growth rate, metabolite yield, or stress response.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Fixed ddG exponential retention/scalar flux, no hydrogen/metal coordination or COBRA redistributed flux network.

text: SBML-compatible engines simulate gene regulatory networks and metabolic pathways, allowing time-resolved analysis of system dynamics under varying environmental conditions (temperature, pH, nutrient availability).
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: SBML-like XML lacks inspected namespace/compartments/stoichiometry/kinetic law; real SBML interpreter compatibility untested.

text: Evolutionary modeling is incorporated through mutation rate simulations, fitness landscapes, and selection pressure modeling, enabling prediction of construct stability, emergence of resistance, and long-term functional decay—one of the most critical unsolved problems in synthetic biology.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Mutation/burden exponential survival, no resistance/emergent construct stability fidelity.

text: SynBio Wizard also acts as a unified biological data infrastructure, integrating heterogeneous datasets from genomic (Ensembl), proteomic (UniProt), and structural (AlphaFold-like) sources into a continuously updating knowledge graph.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Embedded five-product graph live_sourcesFalse, no Ensembl/UniProt/structure continuously updating ingestion.

text: Each node—gene, protein, pathway, or phenotype—is linked through experimentally validated and inferred relationships, enabling cross-layer reasoning from genotype to phenotype.
split_caveat: Automatic punctuation-based unit; abbreviations, formulas and compound sentences may require manual split/merge. No semantic pass implied.
evidence_and_limit: Catalog design-model relationships, not experimentally validated cross-layer reasoning.

text: Experimental outputs (NGS reads, RNA-seq expression profiles, proteomics data) are automatically parsed, normalized, and reintegrated into the system, enabling reinforcement learning from experimental feedback.

evidence_and_limit: Count-level Beta updates from supplied records, no NGS/RNA-seq/proteomics parsing/normalization or RL training.

text: Critically, the system is uncertainty-aware and probabilistic by design.

text: Instead of deterministic outputs, it generates distributions over possible outcomes, incorporating confidence intervals derived from data sparsity, model variance, and experimental noise.

text: The platform can identify regions of high epistemic uncertainty and propose targeted experiments—such as mutational scans, promoter strength libraries, or pathway knockouts—to reduce uncertainty and refine predictions.

text: Molecular docking modules simulate protein–ligand interactions using scoring functions approximating binding affinity (ΔG), while highlighting limitations due to conformational flexibility or solvent effects, preventing overconfidence in purely computational predictions.

text: Ultimately, SynBio Wizard becomes an active discovery engine that closes the loop between design, simulation, and experimentation.

text: It does not merely assist researchers but augments scientific reasoning—generating hypotheses, stress-testing them against multi-scale models, and iteratively refining them through real-world data.

text: By integrating compiler-like abstraction, systems biology modeling, machine learning, and experimental feedback, it transforms synthetic biology into a discipline that is not just descriptive but truly predictive and programmable—capable of engineering biological systems with the same rigor and reproducibility expected in mature engineering fields.
